thread:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency exceeded threshold for /v1/generate in us-west-2. p95=480ms, p99=2800ms, error-rate spike detected. Paging on-call (anne_oncall)

anne_oncall: Got it — I'm on pager. Any immediate mitigation suggestions? Is this service-level or infra?

mike_runtime: Observed streaming stalls — backpressure on runtime layer. We're seeing lots of stalled chunks at the tail. Heap snapshots show KV cache misses rising.

anne_oncall: Can someone drop some recent deploys or config changes? Last deploy window at 1760499000.

eva_prod: No deploys in the last hour. Noticed a flurry of 500s from /controlplane/auth and increased latency to config-service around the same time. Correlating now.

jon_db: Seeing elevated DB tx times for the control-plane DB (auth/flags) — p95 ~ 220ms -> 1.2s. Connection pool saturated on writer nodes. Likely causing downstream stalls.

mike_runtime: Relevant trace sample ( trimmed ):
```
span: request /v1/generate
  -> call: controlplane.auth.validate(token)
    latency: 1.9s
  -> call: config.fetch(model_id)
    latency: 800ms
  -> runtime: kv cache miss, fetch weights
    stall: streaming chunk delayed
```

anne_oncall: So control plane (auth/config/flags) is in the critical path for inference token validation and per-request feature flag evaluation. If DB is slow, that slows the entire inference pipeline.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0314-014. Severity: Sev2. Linked playbook: https://internal.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-0314-014

anne_oncall: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Bypass control-plane synchronous calls where safe (use cached token validation TTL) 2) Temporarily increase control-plane DB pool and promote read replicas if possible 3) Roll traffic to a fallback model variant that uses cached config. Who can flip the config cache fallback?

mike_runtime: I can patch the runtime to short-circuit feature-flag lookup for production-critical routes — add local-read cache and a 500ms timeout to flag fetch. Doing hot patch now.

jon_db: I'll scale DB writer pool and add temporary connection pool increase. Running:
```
-- psql admin commands
ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = 120;
SELECT pg_reload_conf();
```
Will also take a look at slow queries and lock contention.

eva_prod: Customer impact assessment: ~12% of requests to /v1/generate returned >2s and ~0.8% timed out. One enterprise customer (acme-corp) reported timeouts on streaming responses. Support ticket #2341 opened.

anne_oncall: Good. Escalate to db on-call: @jon_db please own DB changes and coordinate with infra. @deploy-bot can we temporarily divert a portion of traffic to us-east-1 to reduce load on us-west-2?

deploy-bot: Routing change queued: shift 25% of traffic to us-east-1 canary. Will take ~60s to propagate.

mike_runtime: Hot patch applied: local feature-flag cache enabled with TTL 30s, 200ms fetch timeout fallback to default. Pushed patch to runtime canary. Logs show immediate reduction in control-plane calls for canary traffic.

jon_db: DB pool scaled. Observing reduced queue depth. Investigating a recent background job that spikes connections — found a nightly job misconfigured to run every 3 minutes. Disabled it.

anne_oncall: Let's measure metrics now — p95/p99 and streaming stall count.

sre-bot: Metric snapshot: before mitigation p95=480ms p99=2800ms streaming_stalls=183/min. After DB scale + cache hotpatch + 25% traffic shift -> p95=220ms p99=360ms streaming_stalls=12/min (rolling 5m).

eva_prod: Confirmed ACME streaming recovery. Support told them to retry, they reported improved behavior. Marked ticket #2341 as "mitigated, monitoring".

anne_oncall: Moving to stabilize: keep DB scaling for 30 minutes, roll out runtime hotpatch to all pods gradually, bake traffic shift back once stable. Also add a temporary circuit breaker so that if control-plane auth exceeds 500ms we fallback to cached decision for 5s.

mike_runtime: Rolling hotpatch cluster-wide with 5% increases every 30s.

jon_db: Monitoring locks and replicas. No further abnormal spikes after disabling job. I'll keep DB scaled and open a follow-up with infra to investigate connection pool defaults.

anne_oncall: Handoff in 30m to the next on-call (mike_runtime will be next). Current incident status: mitigated -> customers recovering. Recording interim incident notes for postmortem.

mike_runtime: Took over on-call. Noted action items: add config-cache in runtime by default, add timeout & fallback for flag fetch, add local token validation TTL logic, add circuit breaker metrics and alert for control-plane latency.

eva_prod: Customer impact summary for postmortem: 1 major enterprise affected intermittently, ~12% requests slowed, no data loss. Financial risk low but SLA credits possible; need review with finance.

anne_oncall: Next steps / post-incident follow-ups (create tickets):
- PROD-FT-102: Add permanent local cache and circuit breaker for control-plane calls (owner: runtime)
- PROD-DB-45: Review DB job scheduling + tune pool defaults (owner: db)
- PROD-MON-77: New alert: control-plane-auth p95 > 300ms -> page eng-sre
- PROD-TEST-88: Add integration test for config-service timeouts + fallback behavior

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-0314-014 marked as mitigated at 1760501600. Postmortem due in 7 days.

anne_oncall: Thanks team. I'll file the postmortem draft and include runbook changes. Closing thread once postmortem created.

mike_runtime: Quick note: in the hotpatch I used this helper for toggling fallback via control-plane API:
```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/flags/toggle \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"runtime_local_cache","value":true}'
```
Make sure ops key use is audited.

jon_db: Follow-up: I'll review DB connection metrics and propose durable pool tuning.

eva_prod: I'll sync with account exec for acme-corp and prepare proactive communications.

anne_oncall: Post-incident priorities: make fallback unintrusive, add metrics to show control-plane dependency latency per request, and ensure rate-limit/auth calls not on critical path for streaming.

mike_runtime: Acknowledged. Closing on-call notes.
